solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Practise piano in private, working out Verdi?

definitions.note: the question mark flags a definition by example: the composer's first name

indicators.note: in places the practise-and-piano pair inside the soldier-and-exercise pair

parts.note: a GI is an American private soldier
PE, physical education, is working out at school
to practise a skill is to use it
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: Advice to rehearse on the keyboard quietly while figuring out how to play Verdi.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Working out' looks like part of the practising, but it is physical education; the soldier and the exercise are split apart to take in the other two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Giuseppe was the forename of the Italian opera composer Verdi, so this is a first-name definition.

clue.text: Our kind, eccentric, European leader of old

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or off-centre, so the letters of our kind are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone describes a quirky continental ruler from history as one of their own kind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eccentric' shuffles only the first two words; the abbreviation for European is added at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The nickname of the Duke of Wellington, the general and prime minister who led Britain long ago.

clue.text: Plant's shoot bore old nodules at the top

parts.note: to snap a picture is to shoot it
a drag is a tedious bore

indicators.note: at the top in a down clue picks the opening letter of nodules

explanation.surface: A gardening note: a plant's new growth has tired old lumps on its tip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant's' reads as possessive but is 'plant is'; shoot is a camera's snap, not a stem.
explanation.definitionFit: The antirrhinum is a garden flower whose blooms open like a mouth, an example of a plant.

clue.text: Watery porridge served here?

parts.note: porridge is British slang for a jail term; one spent at sea is served on a floating jail

explanation.surface: A complaint about thin breakfast oats at some dismal canteen.
explanation.walkthrough: PORRIDGE is British slang for time in prison, and watery means afloat, so the sentence is served on a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A hulk used to hold convicts was a jail afloat, where a sentence, or porridge, was served on water.

clue.text: Pro enters thus, heading off to exercise

indicators.note: enters puts the word for pro inside the trimmed word
heading off drops the first letter of the word for thus

parts.note: hence means thus or therefore
to be for something is to be pro it

explanation.surface: A professional goes in, then sets off to train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' trims the word for thus to ENCE before it takes in the word for pro.
explanation.definitionFit: To exercise authority or a right is to apply it, which is close to imposing a rule.

clue.text: Floppy disc petty officer removed from river

indicators.note: removed from says the disc and officer letters come out of the river

parts.note: the Limpopo is a river of southern Africa
O is disc-shaped, so a disc gives O
PO is the naval abbreviation for petty officer

explanation.surface: A computer disk is lost in a river by a naval officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Floppy disc' reads as one computing term, but floppy is the definition; O and PO leave the end of LIMPOPO.
explanation.definitionFit: Something limp lacks stiffness and hangs loosely, the same as being slack.

clue.text: African tribe, needing tips in Uruguay, unpack ice-pick for climbing

indicators.note: climbing in a down clue means the letters run upward, so they are read backwards
tips in means the end letters of each of the following words

explanation.surface: An African people on a trip to Uruguay unpack a climbing ice-pick.
explanation.walkthrough: The ends of Uruguay, unpack, ice-pick give UYUKIK; 'for climbing' turns this backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kikuyu are the largest ethnic group of Kenya, an East African people.

clue.text: Engineer possessed round mirror with no base

indicators.note: round means the word for possessed goes around the next piece

parts.note: manic means frenzied, as if possessed

indicators.note: in a down clue the base is the last letter, so it is dropped

parts.note: to echo something is to mirror it

explanation.surface: An engineer, in a frenzy, owned a round mirror lacking a stand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no base' drops the bottom letter, as the word is written downwards; the frenzied word then wraps round what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: A fitter who repairs engines and machinery is an engineer in the everyday trade sense.

clue.text: Secure line required for instrument with digital application

parts.note: to nail something down is to secure it
a file is a line of people one behind another

explanation.surface: A secure connection needed for a device with a phone app.
explanation.walkthrough: 'digital' suggests computing, but it means of the fingers.
explanation.definitionFit: An emery board is used on the fingers, digits, so it is a tool applied to the digits.

clue.text: Old woman borne by short strong African

indicators.note: borne by means carried inside the next piece
short cuts off the last letter

parts.note: something solid is strong and firm
ma is slang for mother, one's old woman

explanation.surface: A mother is carried by a stocky, powerful African.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' and 'strong' look like a description of the person; 'short' just trims the last letter of the word for strong.
explanation.definitionFit: Somalis are people from Somalia in the Horn of Africa.

clue.text: Vehicle seen in bad weather currently parking in Berks town

indicators.note: in places the time and parking letters inside the town

parts.note: Slough is a town in Berkshire, England
now means currently
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: A traffic report of a vehicle parked in a Berkshire town during a storm.
explanation.walkthrough: SLOUGH is a commuter town in Berkshire (Berks), west of London.
explanation.definitionFit: A plough-fronted truck clears roads after heavy falls in winter, the vehicle of wintry weather.

clue.text: Sound happy for each individual to be heard

indicators.note: to be heard says the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: per means for each, as in per person

explanation.surface: Make a contented noise so that every person can hear it.
explanation.definitionFit: A cat's contented rumble is the sound it makes when happy.

clue.text: Strangely uncaring, taking non-consecutive articles in Latin

definitions.note: used as a noun: a Latin American

indicators.note: strangely says the letters are put in an odd order

parts.note: two As, the indefinite article twice, not side by side in the result

explanation.surface: Someone oddly indifferent, picking up scattered grammatical articles in a Latin lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in Latin' looks like the classical language; Latin here means Latin American, and 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A citizen of Nicaragua in Central America is a Latino, a Latin American.

clue.text: Dope-smuggling most unusual in high growth area

indicators.note: smuggling means carrying the next piece hidden inside

parts.note: rarest means most unusual
dope is slang for information, info

explanation.surface: Drug-running of a very odd kind in a place where weed grows tall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dope' and 'high growth' suggest drugs; dope means inside information.
explanation.definitionFit: A tropical jungle is a region of tall trees, an area of lofty vegetation.

clue.text: Trucks joined journey over gorge — with effort

parts.note: to go is to journey
to OD is to overdose, and to gorge is to overeat
strain is great effort

explanation.surface: Travelling over a ravine, hard work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' and 'with' only join the pieces in a down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Freight wagons coupled together form a freight locomotive's load.

clue.text: Cut grass and remove weeds? It must be said I'm resigned to it!

indicators.note: it must be said asks for a word taken by sound

parts.note: cut grass is hay, and to remove weeds is to hoe

explanation.surface: A sigh after a day's dull garden chores of mowing and weeding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It must be said' looks like a speaker's aside but signals sound.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation expresses weary acceptance, the sigh of someone accepting their fate.

clue.text: Is supplied with butter and pans

definitions.note: pans here is a verb: criticises

parts.note: to have is to be supplied with
a goat butts, so a goat is a butter

explanation.surface: Kitchen stock: someone has dairy fat and cookware.
explanation.walkthrough: 'butter' is one that butts, a goat, not dairy.
explanation.definitionFit: To pan something is to criticise it harshly, the idiom for attacking verbally.

clue.text: Key I cut out in holiday camp

parts.note: B is a musical key

indicators.note: in puts the trimmed word inside the holiday

parts.note: vac is short for vacation, a holiday

indicators.note: cut means the last letter is removed

explanation.surface: A key the speaker lost on a holiday camp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut out' looks like one verb, but 'cut' trims its last letter from 'out', and the remainder goes inside the word for holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: A temporary encampment without tents, used by soldiers or climbers, is a camp.

clue.text: Emperor, initially awfully unwilling to get up to meet us

indicators.note: initially takes the first letters of the next two words

parts.note: wind is said to gust, or get up, as it rises

explanation.surface: An emperor who at first was very reluctant to rise and greet the people.
explanation.definitionFit: The first Roman emperor took the title Augustus, so he is an emperor by name.

clue.text: Cupboard one used to sweep, keeping neat

indicators.note: keeping means holding the next piece inside

parts.note: a broom is used to sweep
neat is an old word for cattle, so an ox

explanation.surface: A cupboard holding a broom, keeping things tidy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'neat' looks like tidy, but it is the old word for cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: A small storage room in a British house is like a large cupboard.

clue.text: Such a quiet room required by jury?

definitions.meaning: a room insulated so no noise gets in or out
... is solid evidence, which a jury needs to convict

explanation.surface: A silent room the jury must have for deliberating.
explanation.definitionFit: Insulated means noise-tight, and good evidence a jury requires reads as sound proof.

clue.text: Girl had a match not struck?

parts.note: Una is a girl's name
to wed is to make a match in marriage

explanation.surface: A girl married, but her match didn't light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'match' and 'struck' suggest a match being lit; 'struck' means awestruck.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is not awestruck, not impressed, is unafraid and unimpressed.

clue.text: Drop round bringing pudding

parts.note: to sag is to drop or droop
O is a round letter

explanation.surface: Dropping in on someone with a dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: A milk dessert made of starchy palm grains is a classic British school dessert.

clue.text: Successful marksman misses vital run, bagging nothing

indicators.note: bagging means catching the next piece inside

parts.note: misses are girls, gals
O is a zero, nothing
core means central or vital, as in core skills
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A sharpshooter who misses a crucial run and fails to bag anything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misses' looks like failing to hit; it means young women.
explanation.definitionFit: A footballer who puts the ball in the net hits the target, a successful shot.

clue.text: School got by after power cut

indicators.note: cut means the power letter is taken out

parts.note: to cope is to get by, so coped
P is the physics abbreviation for power

explanation.surface: A school managed after a power outage.
explanation.definitionFit: A mixed-sex school, teaching boys and girls together, is co-educational.

clue.text: Bang on front of shield, making demands

parts.note: bang on is British slang for exactly right, exact

indicators.note: front of picks the first letter of shield

explanation.surface: Striking the face of a shield while issuing ultimatums.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bang' looks like a blow; 'bang on' means exactly right.
explanation.definitionFit: To exact payment is to demand it forcefully, so the verb form means requiring.

clue.text: He survived being fired, but has sadly gone on lying

indicators.note: on means the next piece follows on

parts.note: abed means lying in bed

indicators.note: sadly says the letters of gone are put in a sorry order

explanation.surface: A dismissed worker survived the sack, but the unhappy one has gone on lying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fired' suggests sacked; it means thrown into the fiery furnace, in the Book of Daniel.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible he and two companions came out of Nebuchadnezzar's furnace unharmed.

clue.text: Familiarity of film shows that have made English Society

indicators.note: have made English into Society means one E letter is replaced by an S

parts.note: matinees are afternoon film shows

explanation.surface: Afternoon cinema screenings that turned England into high society.
explanation.walkthrough: One E of MATINEES becomes S.
explanation.definitionFit: Being matey means being chummy, so this is the abstract noun for friendliness.
